brief:
The pro-Israel lobby has wielded significant influence over American presidents dating to Harry Truman's administration, the Quincy Institute reported. In 1948, as conflict erupted in Palestine, Truman faced pressure from Zionist lobbyists and others backing the nascent Israeli state, positioning the president between competing political forces during a critical moment in Middle Eastern history.

The influence extended beyond immediate diplomatic decisions, shaping broader U.S. foreign policy orientation toward the region for decades. Truman's experience established a pattern in which successive administrations navigated similar pressures from organized pro-Israel constituencies while managing other strategic interests.

title: Pro-Israel lobby shaped U.S. presidential policy since Truman era
